ai.description: Nanorana mokokchungensis is a small frog (SVL ~30–35 mm) with a brown dorsum and cream-colored venter. It is distinguished by a prominent, dark-spotted throat and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana mokokchungensis* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, prominent blackish-brown longitudinal streaks on its throat, unlike the plain throats of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana mokokchungensis* inhabits high-altitude, fast-flowing hill streams within subtropical broadleaf forests in Nagaland, India, typically at elevations above 1,000m.
ai.behavior: The Mokokchung frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden under rocks or near stream banks during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana mokokchungensis* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), depositing small clutches of eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana mokokchungensis* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Nagaland in Northeast India, specifically found at elevations around 1,300 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nanorana mokokchungensis* consists of a series of high-pitched, rhythmic chirps emitted from within fast-flowing, rocky mountain streams.
